A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. The main text, equations, references, and Appendices A–E are complete and support reliable comparison; v2’s added figures are readable.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical results, mathematical examples, counterexamples, and proofs, but no original experimental or simulation outcomes, including in its appendices.

after.justification: Section 5 and Figure 2 report an original synthetic-data experiment on misspecified multiclass logistic regression, with 100 trials and reported 95% error bars.

M1.justification: The aggregation procedures, surrogate objectives, ranking construction, and nearest-neighbor procedure in Appendix C are retained. Section 5 evaluates instances of the existing framework without changing its method.

E1.justification: v2 adds a narrow synthetic evaluation involving three-class classification in two dimensions with a corrupted logistic link. v1 discusses classification and misspecification theoretically but does not evaluate generated datasets.

E2.justification: The new illustrations include the nonaggregated calibration reference ψ(ε)=ε² in Figure 1 and single-label logistic regression at m=1 in Figure 2. These comparisons were previously theoretical; no additional named competing algorithms are evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a simulation protocol using 10,000 data points per label count, m in {1,4,16,64,256,1024}, and distance between normalized parameter matrices as the outcome. These are settings for a new experiment, not revisions to an existing evaluation.

E4.justification: Section 5 adds targeted numerical checks of aggregation-level sensitivity: Figure 1 illustrates strengthening comparison bounds, while Figure 2 examines parameter-direction recovery under a fixed link misspecification. v1 contains no corresponding numerical robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Figure 2 newly reports 100 trials and 95% error bars. v1 contains no empirical repeated-run or uncertainty reporting. The error-bar construction and random seeds are not specified.

E6.justification: v2 introduces the paper’s first numerical evidence for its central claims. Figure 1 adds calibration-bound curves for several aggregation levels; Figure 2 reports normalized parameter error declining from approximately 0.11 at m=1 to 0.013 at m=1024. These are newly reported outcomes, not same-setting improvements over v1 results.

T1.justification: The existing theorem statements, assumptions, and Appendix A–E proofs are unchanged in substance. Appendix differences are citation and equation renumbering. Section 5’s truncated-quadratic expression directly specializes the retained consistency bound for illustration.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contribution claims retain their scope: aggregation strengthens surrogate consistency and provides robustness under model misspecification. The new numerical illustrations support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 5 qualifies the plotted aggregation bounds as conservative. The expanded discussion identifies quantitative comparison inequalities under restricted hypothesis classes, and their dependence on class size, as a future extension connecting the existing parametric and nonparametric results.

D1.justification: Section 5 and Figure 2 add a simulation recipe: the piecewise corrupted link, true parameter vectors (0,1) and (1,1), radius r=3, and shrinkage factor 0.1, alongside sample and label counts. v1 has no corresponding experimental documentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds six references by Awasthi and colleagues and Mao and colleagues concerning H-consistency, surrogate losses, and growth rates. Added passages distinguish the aggregation-focused contribution from surrogate-focused consistency bounds; the earlier references are retained.

P1.justification: v2 inserts Section 5, Numerical illustrations, renumbers Discussion as Section 6, adds several related-work and future-work passages, and corrects a few typos. The existing narrative and appendix organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds two plots with axes and captions, including a legend in Figure 1 and error bars in Figure 2. Surrounding material reflows, but the single-column format and existing mathematical displays remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the retained theory easier to assess through a concrete calibration illustration, a repeated-trial simulation supporting recovery under misspecification, and clearer positioning against H-consistency research. The empirical evidence covers one synthetic setting, while the existing asymptotic and restricted-class limitations remain, so the overall improvement is limited.
